rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated that no image was available and avoided fabricating specific embryo morphology. It only gave general Day 4 expectations, so it is not inaccurate, but it did not assess the visible embryo, which appears more like a compacting/cavitating morula than a true blastocyst.

It integrated age, PCOS, BMI, ovarian reserve, prior outcomes, sperm parameters, endometrium, and transfer timing into prognosis reasonably well, though some links to embryo-stage-specific implications were somewhat speculative.

The reasoning is structured and mostly internally consistent, with a plausible probability estimate derived from stated factors. Minor issues include speculative interpretation of why Day 4 transfer was chosen and somewhat imprecise quantitative adjustments.

Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based, but several recommendations are not strongly guideline-supported or are controversial/routine only in selected cases (ERA, EMMA/ALICE, NK cells, MTHFR testing, broad thrombophilia workup, and relatively liberal PGT-A suggestion in a 29-year-old).

The response gives clear next steps for luteal support, monitoring, future stimulation strategy, extended culture, and weight management. However, some suggested investigations are overly broad or not well-targeted for this history.
